articles.title: Land Grab in Lucknow? Wall Built on Public Road, Gun Threats and Caste Abuse Alleged in Posh Colony
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A major controversy has erupted in Lucknow’s upscale Swastika City on Sultanpur Road, where residents allege an attempt to illegally occupy a public road using threats in the name of former MP Dhananjay Singh.

body.html:
A major controversy has erupted in Lucknow’s upscale Swastika City on Sultanpur Road, where residents allege an attempt to illegally occupy a public road using threats in the name of former MP Dhananjay Singh.

According to residents, Vinay Singh, husband of Maharajganj (Jaunpur) Block Chief Mandvi Singh, tried to block a 20-foot-wide asphalt road that has been in public use for over 20 years. The road is used daily by women, children and elderly residents. The alleged move was aimed at occupying around 2,000 square feet of disputed land.

On Monday, December 29, Vinay Singh allegedly arrived with his official gunner and 8–10 private guards and began constructing a wall near a house gate, severely restricting movement. When residents objected, he allegedly threatened them, picked up bricks, brandished his licensed rifle and gun, and issued death threats, causing panic in the colony.

During the incident, a youth identified as Ramu was allegedly assaulted with intent to kill and abused with caste-based slurs, following which he fainted. Residents claim videos of the incident have surfaced on social media.

Locals allege Vinay Singh frequently intimidates people by claiming proximity to former MP Dhananjay Singh and even made threatening phone calls during the incident.

Initially, a case was registered on Vinay Singh’s complaint against several colony residents at Sushant Golf City police station, triggering outrage. On December 30, residents met Police Commissioner Amarendra Singh Sengar, after which an FIR was registered under 11 sections against Vinay Singh, Dhananjay Singh, Vinay Singh’s gunner, and several unidentified persons.

Residents allege the land is already under dispute among three parties and is sub judice, but Vinay Singh is attempting to gain access by encroaching on the road. Police investigation is ongoing.

articles.title: Dismissed RAC Jawan Caught in Burqa and Lipstick After R*ping Minor in Rajasthan
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Police have arrested a dismissed Railway Protection Force (RAC) jawan who was absconding after allegedly r*ping a 16-year-old girl in Dholpur district, Rajasthan, on 15th December.

body.html:
Police have arrested a dismissed Railway Protection Force (RAC) jawan who was absconding after allegedly r*ping a 16-year-old girl in Dholpur district, Rajasthan, on 15th December. The accused, 50-year-old Rajendra Sisodiya, was caught in Vrindavan, Uttar Pradesh, disguised in a woman's burqa with lipstick on and a shaved head.

Dholpur SP Vikas Sangwan said the accused lured the victim and her brother to his house, promising a job in Railway Police. He met the girl's father at a hospital and gained his trust. On 15th December, he called the minor to his residence on the pretext of providing job forms. When her younger brother accompanied her, Sisodiya sent him away to photocopy documents and allegedly r*ped the girl before fleeing.

The Kushwaha community protested and pressured authorities for swift action. Police announced a ₹10,000 reward, and Dholpur Municipal Council demolished part of the accused's house. BJP and Congress leaders held separate panchayats on 28th December, with former MLA BL Kushwaha warning of protests from 4th January.

SP Sangwan revealed Sisodiya is a notorious criminal with five prior cases including POCSO, kidnapping, and assault. He evaded capture by changing identities—posing as a police inspector, retired deputy SP, and wearing different disguises. On 28th December, police grew suspicious of a person walking like a woman in Vrindavan. Upon chase, Sisodiya was caught and his burqa removed, revealing his disguise. Police paraded him through Dholpur streets after arrest. Interrogation is ongoing.

articles.title: From r*pe Claim to Molestation: BJP Leader Arrested as Case Takes Dramatic Turn in Satna
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A major twist has emerged in the s*xual assault case involving BJP leader Ashok Singh from Rampur Baghelan in Madhya Pradesh’s Satna district. The woman who had earlier accused him of raping her at knifepoint and filming the act has now withdrawn her r*pe allegation.

body.html:
A major twist has emerged in the s*xual assault case involving BJP leader Ashok Singh from Rampur Baghelan in Madhya Pradesh’s Satna district. The woman who had earlier accused him of raping her at knifepoint and filming the act has now withdrawn her r*pe allegation.

On Saturday night, the complainant told the police that she was not r*ped but was molested and subjected to obscene remarks. Based on her revised statement, the police arrested Ashok Singh.

Sub-Inspector Preeti Kushwaha said the woman submitted a written application stating that her earlier r*pe complaint and allegations of threats were made in anger and fear. She clarified that the accused had molested her and made obscene gestures.

Following this, a case was registered against Ashok Singh under sections 74 (outraging the modesty of a woman), 75(2) (s*xual harassment), 79 (insult by word or gesture), 296(1) (obscene act), and 351(3) (criminal intimidation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Police said the victim’s security has been ensured.

Earlier, on December 22, the woman had approached SP Hansraj Singh, alleging that Ashok Singh, a resident of Karhi whose wife is a councillor, had entered her house six months ago, r*ped her at knifepoint, recorded a video, and blackmailed her by threatening to make it viral.

The case drew attention after a video of the accused surfaced on social media on Friday, in which he was seen challenging the police and claiming that no action could be taken against him. Following public outrage and media coverage, the police intensified action, leading to his arrest a day later, even as the complainant altered her statement.

Ashok Singh (50), son of Laxminarayan Singh, has a long criminal record spanning nearly three decades. Police records show that nine cases have been registered against him since 1996, including grievous assault, rioting, obstructing government work, house trespass, extortion, criminal intimidation, and use of abusive and obscene language. In 2025, a case of criminal breach of trust was also registered against him under the BNS.

The investigation in the case is ongoing.

articles.title: LPG Cylinder Blast Turns House Into Death Trap in Muzaffarnagar, Three of Family Charred
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Three members of a family were burnt to death after a fire broke out in their house followed by an LPG cylinder explosion at Vasundhara Residency under Nai Mandi police station in Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, on Monday.

body.html:
Three members of a family were burnt to death after a fire broke out in their house followed by an LPG cylinder explosion at Vasundhara Residency under Nai Mandi police station in Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh, on Monday.

The deceased were identified as Amit Gaur (50), a kanungo posted in Deoband tehsil (earlier reported as Saharanpur), his mother Sushila (68), and younger brother Nitin Gaur (45). The family was living on the second floor of the building in rented accommodation.

Eyewitnesses said the fire started around 5.30 pm and within minutes, LPG cylinders exploded, engulfing the entire house in flames. Amit, his mother and brother were trapped inside and died on the spot.

Four others — Richa, Akshika, Aradhya and Noni — sustained severe burn injuries and were admitted to hospital, where their condition is reported to be critical.

SP City Satyanarayan Prajapat said police, fire brigade and administrative teams rushed to the spot after receiving information through the control room. During rescue operations, three bodies were recovered from the house.

Preliminary investigation suggests the fire started inside the house. Remains of two LPG cylinders and an angithi (portable stove) were found at the scene. The bodies have been sent for post-mortem and further investigation is underway.

articles.title: ‘Move the Car or I’ll Beat You’: Viral Video Shows Woman Claiming to Be Cop Assaulting Couple
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A video showing a woman, claiming to be a police inspector, assaulting a couple inside a car on Abu Lane in Meerut has gone viral on social media. The incident took place on Sunday (28 December 2025) amid heavy traffic congestion on Abu Lane.

body.html:
A video showing a woman, claiming to be a police inspector, assaulting a couple inside a car on Abu Lane in Meerut has gone viral on social media.

The incident took place on Sunday (28 December 2025) amid heavy traffic congestion on Abu Lane. The woman arrived in an i20 car bearing registration number UP22X7788, with a police cap placed on the dashboard. According to the video, she became enraged after another car stopped in front of her vehicle.

She was heard threatening the couple, saying she would beat them with a belt if they did not move the car. The woman then stepped out, opened the car door of the vehicle ahead, and verbally abused the occupants. When the woman inside the car objected, she too was abused.

The woman allegedly assaulted the man and threatened to send him to jail if he resisted. A crowd gathered at the spot as the altercation escalated, and passersby who tried to intervene were also treated rudely. The incident was captured by bystanders on mobile phones.

Senior Superintendent of Police Dr Vipin Tada said the woman involved is being identified and appropriate legal action will be taken after verification.

articles.title: Pregnant Woman’s Death Sparks Murder Allegations Against In-Laws in UP Village
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: An eight-month pregnant woman, Kanak alias Kamal, wife of Ashish, died under suspicious circumstances around 11 pm on Saturday in Dhanaura Tikri village of Bagpat district, Uttar Pradesh.

body.html:
An eight-month pregnant woman, Kanak alias Kamal, wife of Ashish, died under suspicious circumstances around 11 pm on Saturday in Dhanaura Tikri village of Bagpat district, Uttar Pradesh.

After receiving the information, her parents from Parasauli village reached the spot and accused Kanak’s in-laws of murdering her, alleging the incident was linked to her opposition to her husband’s alleged illicit relationship. Her mother Rekha, brother Ravi and niece Tanu reportedly created a ruckus while making the allegations.

Doghat police station in-charge Suryadeep Singh said the body has been sent for post-mortem in Bagpat and further action will be taken based on the report. Police have secured the scene and started an investigation.

No arrests have been made so far, as police are awaiting the autopsy report to confirm the cause of death. The in-laws have been detained for questioning.
